newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BT confident of EU clearance for MCI deal.
newsitem.headline: BT confident of EU clearance for MCI deal.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc said on Monday it was optimistic the European Commission would clear its merger with the second largest U.S. telecommunications company MCI.

Larry Stone, BT's head of European Union affairs, told Reuters he hoped the deal would be dealt with under the EU's fast-track merger rules and did not anticipate any anti-trust problems because the companies "operate in competitive markets".
"One of the clearances we will be seeking is the European Commission's. We're confident that will be forthcoming," Stone said.
BT and MCI announced on Sunday they would merge their operations in their existing joint venture Concert in a $20 billion deal.
Stone said the Commission was given "all the relevant press and public material" on the operation the same day. BT would also be talking with Commission officials "imminently".
He thought the deal would fall under the merger regulation which allows for EU clearance within a month of the deal being notified if it does not create competition problems.

When it assessed the Concert venture in 1993, the Commission said it was not a concentration and instead examined it under article 85 of the EU treaty which forbids concerted practices and behaviour that harms fair competition.

Stone said that was because MCI's turnover in the Union was below the threshold set in the merger regulation, which is 250 million European currency units. He said the two companies were assessing the current turnover figure.

The spokesman for European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said on Monday the Commission would assess the merger between BT and MCI, but declined to speculate on the legal basis that will be used and whether the deal posed any competition fears.
"The only thing I can say is that it will have to be examined by the Commission," the spokesman said in reply to reporters's questions. "I'm not saying it looks complicated or not," he added.

There is no strict deadline for ruling on joint ventures falling under the highly unpopular article 85 and the Commission's decision -- a comfort letter if no competition problems arise -- does not give the companies involved the legal certainty that the deal has passed all anti-trust tests.

The Concert venture was granted a seven-year exemption from EU competition rules which will last until November 15, 2000, at which time the companies can seek a renewal. It is unclear how this may be affected by the full merger.
It was the first joint venture in the telecommunications sector to have cleared all the regulatory procedures around the world.
Since then, the Commission has cleared with conditions the Global One alliance between France Telecom, Deutsche Telekom and Sprint Corp of the United States.
It is also vetting a joint venture between Unisource, a grouping of four European telecoms operators, and AT&T Corp.
Concert was originally created to provide value added and enhanced telecoms services to large multinational corporations.

But the full opening of the European telecoms market to competition in January 1998 creates vast business opportunities including in the traditional telephone sector which is still to a large extent controlled by national monopolies.
